## Watchdog status check 2026-11-16: not built/deployed — this week's Mistral outage is the acceptance case

Checking in from the Mistral quota outage of 2026-11-13 → 2026-11-16 (full record on #6033): **the watchdog core in this issue does not exist as a running thing today.** On the laptop as of 2026-11-16 there is no quota-watchdog systemd unit or timer, no `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/quota-watchdog-state.json`, and no standalone Mistral producer under `~/atlas/` — the only Mistral read path is the gatherer's `opencode quota --json` leg. This issue was closed as completed on 2026-11-09, found WRONGLY CLOSED by the 90-day review, reopened 2026-11-14, and is currently `status/parked`.

Consequence, concretely: the Mistral console read failed `cdp-unavailable` on every gatherer tick for ~57 hours (last good read 2026-11-13T22:10:15Z). The failure matched this design's own classes (browser killed by a laptop reboot, then a wrong-profile browser with no session — which also exposed that the reader misclassifies a login bounce as `cdp-unavailable` instead of `session-expired`). No repair was attempted and no incident was escalated by any automation; a human-dispatched repair fixed it on 2026-11-16 (fresh read 2026-11-16T07:06:24Z). The one stale-source note that did fire (quota-check v71, 2026-11-14) produced no repair dispatch — that conversion step is #6033's territory and it also never landed as a running loop.

Until this watchdog (or at least a supervised unit for the CDP browser) exists, every laptop reboot silently re-breaks the browser-dependent quota reads.

**Watchdog partial landing — the CDP browser is now supervised (2026-11-16 ~01:20 CST)**

Follow-up to the repair on #6033 (comment 6909868442) and the verdict on this issue (comment 6909869155): the relaunched Helium CDP browser was a bare nohup and would have died silently at the next laptop reboot, exactly like the 2026-11-13 19:28 CST reboot that darkened the Mistral read for ~57h. It is now under supervision.

**Built**
- `helium-cdp.service` (systemd user unit, `~/.config/systemd/user/helium-cdp.service`), enabled under `default.target`; linger is on for the user, so it starts at boot. `Restart=always`, `RestartSec=3`.
- It runs the exact configuration the repair verified live: `/run/current-system/sw/bin/helium --headless=new --remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1 --remote-debugging-port=19222 --user-data-dir=/home/user/.config/net.imput.helium --no-first-run --disable-gpu --disable-extensions --noerrdialogs`. The profile is the real Helium profile carrying the live Mistral admin session — NOT the ChatGPT profile copy. The unit-managed process's command line is byte-identical to the verified working instance.
- Adoption: the bare nohup (pid 2881662) was killed, the port/profile freed, and the unit started fresh (MainPID 2912511). No dual-browser fight over port 19222 or the profile.
- `~/atlas/launch-helium-cdp.sh` fixed: it previously hardcoded the wrong profile (`~/atlas/helium-chatgpt-profile-copy`, the cause of the Nov 15 misdiagnosis) and lacked `--disable-extensions`. It now delegates to `systemctl --user start helium-cdp.service` and documents the trap in-script; the old script is kept as `launch-helium-cdp.sh.bak-20261116`.

**Recovery proof (live)**
- `kill -9` on the unit's browser (pid 2912511) → systemd restarted it: NRestarts=1, new MainPID 2923898, port 19222 listening again, CDP `/json/version` answering.
- A gatherer tick was then run (`quota-gatherer.service`, started 2026-11-16T07:19:17Z, exit 0). `quota-current.json` Mistral entry: `state: "ok"`, **measuredAt 2026-11-16T07:19:25.600Z**, heartbeat ok, no `retainedFromFailedTick`. The Mistral session survived the unit-managed restart — no login page, no sign-in needed.

**What remains of this issue's original scope (NOT built — do not close on this comment)**
Process supervision guarantees the browser is alive and restarted; it does not detect a *stale read while the browser lives*. Still missing from the original watchdog scope:
1. Stale-read detection + escalation: if ticks start failing (e.g. the Mistral session eventually expires and the scrape lands on a login page) or the browser wedges while still listening on 19222, nothing yet notices, retries beyond the gatherer's own tick, or escalates — that was the silent failure mode for the back half of the 57h outage.
2. A liveness probe that exercises CDP (not just process existence) with a supervised restart on a wedged endpoint.

Leaving this issue open (status/parked) for that remainder.
